facts.statement: All six tb2 Nav2 nodes and its lifecycle manager were launched.
tb2 planner_server reported a change_state response-send timeout in rmw_response.cpp.
tb3 controller reported a get_state response-send timeout, then all tb3 readiness deficits disappeared; the final logged deficit list contains only tb2.
tb2 controller, planner, behavior, bt_navigator, waypoint_follower and velocity_smoother each exited cleanly during shutdown; no native crash for these nodes appears in the captured log.
tb2 lifecycle manager required SIGTERM and SIGKILL and exited -9; this remains an infrastructure failure.
The exploration task was not released and no native seed303 evaluation JSON exists; runner failure cannot count as task success or safety evidence.

facts.evidence: nav2_ready_gate.py lines74-80 in recorded source SHA
facts.statement: Lifecycle GetState requests are issued only after the robot NavigateToPose action is ready. Default unavailable labels for tb2 therefore do not prove all six lifecycle services are absent.

The same frozen source and robot parameter files reached all-three-Nav2-active readiness in corridors seeds101 and202. No general deterministic launch/configuration ordering bug is established by seed303.

hypotheses_not_proven: Stale FastDDS shared-memory resources may have contributed; no SHM/open_and_lock or memory-exhaustion diagnostic was found in the nine captured version2 logs.
Parallel Gazebo/Nav2 load may have contributed to discovery or scheduling delays; this attempt has no CPU, queue, or DDS-discovery trace proving that cause.
The default unbounded Nav2 transition response wait may explain the stalled manager and forced shutdown; no thread stack proves its exact blocked call in this attempt.
